page.layout: One page of text, one column. Theses numbered in Roman numerals, each followed by its text. No marginal notes, no running head, no page number printed.

main_text.p: XXXI. Neq; propterea aut ternio scientiarum perit: aut illa Universalis esse definit scientia. contra Scot. scrup. & spinos.hom.
XXXII. At quid de Mentibus separatis? Et principis Subiecti locum his quidem magni Viri condonari volut[?]; & in Subiecti quoq; principijs ponere.
XXXIII. Ast quomodo? Sapietia Ens, in principia, & ea qua[?] inde exsurgunt deductum subijciunt: illud vero Intelligentia, hoc autem Scientia committunt. 6. Ethic. c.3.6.7. Comm.
XXXIV. Poterat inde φιλοσοφήματα[?] plurima hauriri; sed PHYSICA iam admonet de tabula manum.
XXXV. PHYSICA. Scientia sane ut per se expetibilis: sic omnibus insuper disciplinis & cōmodo & ornameto futura. D.Sut.Dial rer.nat,c.1.
XXXVI. Altera igitur Philosophia merito dicta. substatia[?].n.hæc Naturalis, quâ talis est, principia docet, caussarum p.partium, affectionum & proprietatum eiusdem contemplatrix. 4.Metaphys.t.4.
XXXVII. De cuius Subiecto plures quastiones[?] sunt, quâ difficul-tates.
XXXIIX. Subiectum Philosophiæ Naturalis siue Ens mobile, siue corpus mobile, siue corpus naturale dixeris, siue substātiam naturalem, vel etiam substantiam sensibilem, nihil absurdi consequetur.
XXXIX. Physicum porrò corpus dixero; si modò in eo Naturâ suæ

page.notes: The number before the 38th thesis is printed "XXXIIX" (sequence error for XXXVIII); left as printed. "volut", "Neq;", "substatia", "quastiones" and "qua" before "in-de" are doubtful readings, marked [?]. The Greek word in XXXIV ("φιλοσοφήματα") is partly unclear; marked [?]. The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page with "suæ" and continues on the next page. "Intelligentia" and "p.partium" are written whole as printed line-breaks show no hyphen.
